bull.b: Term-based subscriptions create recurring revenue and support durable customer relationships. The cloud-native delivery model can also enable efficient upselling across users, products, modules, geographies, and business units as customers broaden their security coverage.

Growth in larger customer cohorts indicates increasing enterprise penetration and platform adoption. More high-value accounts can support durable expansion through broader deployments, larger contracts, and cross-selling beyond Zscaler’s initial product purchase.

Strong cash conversion despite accounting losses gives Zscaler resources to fund product development, infrastructure, and go-to-market investment internally. Persistently high gross margins also provide a foundation for operating leverage as the platform scales.

bear.b: Ongoing GAAP losses show that the company has not yet converted its strong gross margins and recurring revenue base into bottom-line profitability. Sustained losses can constrain measured earnings quality and leave execution dependent on continued growth and expense discipline.

The lower forward growth outlook suggests that the exceptionally rapid expansion of fiscal 2026 may not persist at the same rate. Slower ARR and revenue growth could reduce operating leverage, moderate platform adoption momentum, and raise the importance of successful new product execution.

Elevated spending on data-center infrastructure and Zero Trust Branch appliances can pressure near-term free cash flow and delay cash-margin improvement. Higher investment may support capacity and innovation, but it increases execution demands and reduces flexibility if growth moderates.
